## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saraṇattaya* ("The Three Refuges", also cited as *Saraṇattayam* or *Trīṇiśaraṇāni*) is the opening text of the *Khuddakapāṭha* in the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Canon [Hazra 1994; Piyadassi 1979; Williams and Ladwig 2012]. It sets forth the basic formula of taking refuge in the Three Jewels (Buddha, Dhamma, and Saṅgha), serving as an elementary training, a resolution, and an act of devotional veneration [Piyadassi 1979]. Beyond its standing as the first lesson of the *Khuddakapāṭha*, the text also opens the traditional *paritta* protection and recitation collections, including the *Catubhāṇavārapāḷi* [Anālayo 2018; Williams and Ladwig 2012].

 DharmaNexus matches the entirety of the text (§§1.1–4.3) with Kd 1 (§§12.4.1–12.4.9) with identical similarity (1.0), and records further reuse in the commentary, the *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā* (§§1.1–3.1 ↔ §§4–7) [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: Kd 1 Mahākhandhaka
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1) (§1.1–4.3 ↔ §12.4.1–12.4.9); Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0501a) (§1.1–3.1 ↔ §4–7)
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Segment-level matches and character similarity scores with Kd 1 and Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Identifies the text as the first lesson of the Khuddakapāṭha and discusses its derivation from the Khandhakas
- [Piyadassi 1979] Piyadassi Thera, ed., Felicitation Volume to Narada Mahathera (1979) — Discusses the function and alternative designations of the formula (Tisaraṇa-gamana, Trīṇiśaraṇāni)
- [Williams and Ladwig 2012] Paul S. Williams and Patrice Ladwig, Buddhist Funeral Cultures of Southeast Asia and China (2012) — Notes the order of texts in the Khuddakapāṭha liturgy
- [Anālayo 2018] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Rebirth in Early Buddhism & Current Research (2018) — Documents the inclusion of Saraṇattaya at the beginning of the Catubhāṇavārapāḷi collection
